declaration: composite-unique: Columns datasource_name, workspace_id must be unique
subject: t_st_datasource(datasource_name, workspace_id)
rationale: [Columns datasource_name, workspace_id must be unique] Sequential duplicates are rejected by the application pre-check checkDatasourceNameUnique (code 60004 'datasource [..] already exists'), which is scoped to the current workspace. The pre-check is not atomic: under 6 concurrent creates of the same name, several requests passed the SELECT and reached the INSERT, where H2 raised 23505 'Unique index or primary key violation: CONSTRAINT_INDEX_E ON public.t_st_datasource(datasource_name, workspace_id)'. Exactly one row per name persisted; the DB rejection was surfaced as generic code 99999 with the raw SQL message. The DB is therefore the actual guarantee and its rejection is unhandled. The application's pre-check is non-atomic and is bypassed (see the race/rename cases), so it does not enforce the predicate; enforcement is provided by the database.
limitations: Race outcome is timing dependent; observed in 2 of 3 rounds.;Log slices for concurrent cases overlap.

subject: t_st_datasource(datasource_config)
rationale: [t_st_datasource.datasource_config has length 1023] A value of length > 1023 for t_st_datasource.datasource_config passed through the controller/service without any length check and reached the INSERT/UPDATE (SQL trace shows the statement being prepared with the oversized parameter). H2 rejected it with JdbcSQLDataException 22001 'Value too long for column "datasource_config CHARACTER VARYING(1023)"'; GlobalExceptionHandler turned it into HTTP 200 with generic code 99999 'Unknown exception' and leaked the raw SQL/driver message. A boundary value of exactly 1023 characters was accepted where tested. The request map is serialised to JSON by the service before insert; the serialised length (1122) exceeded 1023.
